notes: Overall a solid implementation with good separation of concerns and clean TypeScript. Issues found: (1) ARCHITECTURAL VIOLATION - main.ts wires the comment.added event handler by calling this.taskService.getById() directly inside the Application class, which acts as a hidden cross-service dependency rather than true event-driven decoupling; the notification logic for comments requires task data that isn't carried in the event payload, forcing a direct service call. (2) ARCHITECTURAL VIOLATION - CommentService receives a getUserName callback injected at construction time that calls userService.getById() internally — this is effectively a disguised cross-service call, violating Rule 1, even if indirect. (3) The CommentAddedPayload has an empty taskTitle field (set to '') that is never populated, meaning comment notifications don't include the task title, indicating incomplete event payload design. (4) The router correctly owns all HTTP handling and services own their own stores — those rules are followed well. (5) Forward-only status transitions are correctly implemented with a clear transition map. (6) No external npm dependencies are used; crypto is a Node.js built-in. (7) Each service is in its own file. (8) GET /tasks requires projectId query param, meaning you can't retrieve a single arbitrary task list without a project — this is a minor API design limitation but not a spec violation. (9) demo.ts uses require('http') inside an async function instead of a top-level import, which is a minor style issue. (10) Error handling uniformly converts thrown errors to 500 responses without distinguishing 404 (not found) from 400 (bad input) — all service-level errors return 500. (11) The unused variable warning in comment-service.ts delete method (const comment = this.getById(id) is assigned but only used for side-effect validation). (12) test.ts is a good smoke test but not a proper test suite with assertions framework. The core architecture is mostly correct but the cross-service coupling issues in the comment notification flow are meaningful violations.
